account:
Today has mostly been ordinary town business. I attended morning office hours and the ten o'clock market walk, and am now home following my noon lunch appointment. I must return to town hall for the one o'clock accounts review, meet the neighbour at the dockside cottage at three, and attend office at half past four.

The only mildly unusual report concerns bakery lights. The neighbour heard others mention them, but did not observe anything unusual personally and says the baker knows of no special occasion. The baker reportedly says fresh bread is coming to market. Townsfolk Ten reported the baker carrying a sack of bread at the bridge; the secretary also saw the baker near the bridge around ten thirty-six carrying bread, without establishing a destination or companion. I later saw the baker near the bridge holding emeralds and heard a distant shout whose words I could not understand. None of this establishes a secret gathering or wrongdoing. Supplying the market is a straightforward possible explanation for the bread and lights. The secretary has received no reports of shortages or unusual evening activity. The neighbour offered to observe the docks on the way home and tell me anything actually seen at tea.

The builder is inspecting the bridge without spending or altering anything and is due to bring repair priorities and separate materials and labour estimates to the one o'clock review. No defects have yet been confirmed and I have authorized no expenditure. I should keep this routine inspection distinct from rumours of a bridge problem. For now I have a few bakery-related observations, but no evidence of what, if anything, is happening without me.
